questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a coordinating conjunction to express a result?
choices: The game was postponed because the downpour flooded the field.
The downpour flooded the field, so the game was postponed.
If the downpour flooded the field, the game was postponed.
Although the downpour flooded the field, the game was postponed.
questions.explanation: The coordinating conjunction so joins two independent clauses and signals that the game's postponement resulted from the flooding.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the comparative correlative construction the more..., the fewer...?
choices: The more carefully the editor read the draft, the fewer errors he found.
The more carefully the editor read the draft, fewer errors he found.
The more the editor carefully read the draft, the fewer errors he found.
The editor read the draft the more carefully, the fewer errors he found.
questions.explanation: The comparative correlative construction places the more clause first and the fewer clause second to show a linked relationship.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a causal subordinate clause to explain why the lights came on?
choices: The lights came on because the power was restored.
The lights came on although the power was restored.
The lights came on before the power was restored.
The lights came on when the power was restored.
questions.explanation: Because introduces a causal subordinate clause that identifies the restoration of power as the reason the lights came on.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly adds a nonrestrictive clause about the scientist?
choices: The scientist, who had won three awards, explained the results.
The scientist who had won three awards explained the results.
After the scientist had won three awards, the scientist explained the results.
The scientist explained the results, who had won three awards.
questions.explanation: The commas mark who had won three awards as supplementary information about the scientist.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a that-clause as the direct object of knew?
choices: The engineers knew when the bridge needed repairs.
The engineers knew the bridge needed repairs.
The engineers knew because the bridge needed repairs.
The engineers knew that the bridge needed repairs.
questions.explanation: The that-clause containing the bridge needed repairs functions as the direct object of knew.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an it-cleft construction to foreground the cause of the delay?
choices: It was the missing key that delayed the rehearsal.
The missing key delayed the rehearsal.
The rehearsal was delayed because the key was missing.
There was a missing key delaying the rehearsal.
questions.explanation: The it-cleft construction places the cause in the focus of the sentence after the phrase It was.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a balanced two-clause pattern with the same subject and a parallel active verb in each clause?
choices: The club raised money at the bake sale, and the club bought books for the elementary school.
The club raised money at the bake sale, and the books for the elementary school were bought with those funds.
The club raised money at the bake sale, although it also bought books for the elementary school.
After raising money at the bake sale, the club bought books for the elementary school.
questions.explanation: The two independent clauses have matching subject-predicate structures and comparable lengths, creating a balanced pattern.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a compound subject with a plural verb?
choices: The coach and the team celebrated the unexpected victory.
The coach and the team was celebrated the unexpected victory.
The coach and the team has celebrated the unexpected victory.
The coach and the team were celebrate the unexpected victory.
questions.explanation: The compound subject coach and the team correctly takes the plural verb celebrated.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a concessive clause to express a contrast that weakens the expected result?
choices: If the trail was muddy, the runners reached the summit.
Because the trail was muddy, the runners reached the summit.
Although the trail was muddy, the runners reached the summit.
The runners reached the summit while the trail was muddy.
questions.explanation: Although introduces a concessive clause that contrasts the muddy trail with the runners' success.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses anticipatory it, placing the real subject in a that-clause after the verb?
choices: That the two plans have different costs is obvious.
It was the two plans that had different costs.
It is obvious that the two plans have different costs.
The difference in cost between the two plans is obvious.
questions.explanation: The opening it is an anticipatory subject, while that the two plans have different costs is the clause supplying the real subject.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an inverted subject-verb structure to emphasize the setting?
choices: The comet streaked across the bright field.
A bright comet streaked across the field.
Across the field, a bright comet streaked.
Across the field streaked a bright comet.
questions.explanation: The prepositional phrase Across the field comes first, placing the subject a bright comet before the verb streaked.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence has an introductory dependent clause followed by two independent clauses joined by a comma and a coordinating conjunction?
choices: When the bell rang, the students entered the gym; the coaches began arranging the stations.
When the bell rang the students entered the gym, and the coaches began arranging the stations.
The students entered the gym when the bell rang, and the coaches began arranging the stations.
When the bell rang, the students entered the gym, and the coaches began arranging the stations.
questions.explanation: The sentence opens with a dependent clause, and its two independent clauses are joined by a comma followed by the coordinating conjunction and.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence is complex, containing one independent clause and one dependent clause?
choices: The power failed during the rehearsal, and the lights remained on throughout the hall.
The power failed during the rehearsal, but the lights remained on throughout the hall.
The power failed, and although the lights remained on, the rehearsal continued.
Although the power failed, the lights remained on throughout the rehearsal.
questions.explanation: Although the power failed is a dependent clause, while the lights remained on throughout the rehearsal is an independent clause.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly places a comma after an introductory dependent clause?
choices: Before the first act began, the audience, settled into their seats.
Before the first act began the audience settled into their seats.
Before the first act began, the audience settled into their seats.
Before, the first act began, the audience settled into their seats.
questions.explanation: A comma separates the introductory dependent clause Before the first act began from the main clause.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a noun clause as its complete subject?
choices: The team discovered what changed the final plan.
What the team discovered changed the final plan.
What the team discovered was changed the final plan.
The discovery that the team made changed the final plan.
questions.explanation: The entire clause What the team discovered functions as the subject of the verb changed.
questions.skill: Use a noun clause as a subject
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a pair of em dashes to set off an interruption?
choices: The finalists—nervous despite the applause, answered each question.
The finalists—nervous despite the applause—answered each question.
The finalists, nervous despite the applause—answered each question.
The finalists: nervous despite the applause—answered each question.
questions.explanation: The paired em dashes correctly set off the interrupting phrase nervous despite the applause.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a that-clause as a subject complement?
choices: The team's conclusion was that the map was incomplete.
The team's conclusion was because the map was incomplete.
The team's conclusion was if the map was incomplete.
The team's conclusion was the map was incomplete.
questions.explanation: The that-clause that the map was incomplete functions as the subject complement of conclusion.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains three independent clauses joined by coordinating conjunctions?
choices: The wind died down, the team returned to the field, and the game resumed.
After the wind died down, the team returned to the field, and the game resumed.
The wind died down, the team returned to the field, because the game resumed.
The wind died down, the team returned to the field, but the game resumed.
questions.explanation: The clauses about the wind, the team, and the game are all independent and are joined with the coordinating conjunctions and and and.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence places an indirect object immediately before the direct object?
choices: The librarian handed to the student a bookmark.
The librarian handed the student a bookmark.
The librarian handed the bookmark to the student.
The librarian handed a bookmark to the student.
questions.explanation: The noun phrase the student functions as the indirect object, and the noun phrase a bookmark functions as the direct object.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an adjective as an object complement?
choices: The audience found the performance a complete failure.
The audience found the performance to be unforgettable.
The audience found very unforgettable the performance.
The audience called the performance unforgettable.
questions.explanation: The adjective unforgettable describes what the audience called the performance and therefore functions as the object complement.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the degree-result pattern so...that?
choices: The storm was so severe the roads were closed.
The storm was such severe that the roads were closed.
The storm was very severe that the roads were closed.
The storm was so severe that the roads were closed.
questions.explanation: The correlative pair so...that expresses degree and result, linking the storm's severity to the road closures.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence has a periodic structure, with its main clause following an introductory dependent clause?
choices: After the final whistle blew and the players left the field, the referee recorded the score.
The final whistle blew, the players left the field, and the referee recorded the score.
The referee recorded the score after the final whistle blew, and the players left the field.
After recording the score, the final whistle blew and the players left the field.
questions.explanation: The introductory dependent clause delays the main clause, the referee recorded the score, until the end of the sentence.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a gerund phrase after a preposition to modify the subject?
choices: After the straps were tightened, the climbers tested each knot.
Before using the new equipment, the instructions were posted.
After tightening the straps, their knots were tested.
After tightening the straps, the climbers tested each knot.
questions.explanation: The gerund phrase tightening the straps logically modifies the subject climbers and makes their action occur before the knot testing.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence is compound-complex because it contains two independent clauses and one dependent clause?
choices: After the rehearsal ended, the actors bowed, and the lights came on.
Because the road was flooded, we took a longer route.
The lights came on, and the actors bowed.
The lights came on before the actors bowed in front of the audience.
questions.explanation: The sentence contains the dependent clause After the rehearsal ended and the two independent clauses the actors bowed and the lights came on.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence begins with a fronted prepositional phrase followed by a main clause in standard subject-verb order?
choices: Around the corner glowed the old theater before sunset.
Before the old theater glowed, around the corner the evening deepened.
Around the corner, the old theater glowed before sunset.
The old theater around the corner glowed before sunset.
questions.explanation: The prepositional phrase Around the corner is fronted, and the main clause follows in the standard subject-verb order.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a compound direct object and a prepositional phrase instead of an indirect object?
choices: The coach gave the team water and towels.
The coach gave water and towels to the team.
The coach gave the team a water bottle and towels.
The coach gave water to the team and towels to the bench.
questions.explanation: Water and towels form a compound direct object, and to the team identifies the recipient without using an indirect object.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a relative clause with the object relative pronoun correctly omitted?
choices: The book you recommended was difficult to follow.
The book whom you recommended was difficult to follow.
The book you was recommended was difficult to follow.
The book who you recommended was difficult to follow.
questions.explanation: In the relative clause you recommended, the object relative pronoun can be omitted because its role is already understood from the verb.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a colon to introduce a list of three items?
choices: The supply list included three items; a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
The supply list included three items—a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
The supply list included three items: a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
The supply list included three items, including a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
questions.explanation: The colon correctly introduces the list a notebook, a pen, and a folder.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a past participle correctly as a subject-complement adjective?
choices: The finalists were prepared to answer every question.
The finalists were prepare to answer every question.
The finalists were preparation to answer every question.
The finalists was prepared to answer every question.
questions.explanation: Prepared is a past participle used as an adjective to describe the finalists' state before answering questions.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a colon to introduce an explanatory clause?
choices: The plan had one flaw, it ignored the morning traffic.
The plan had one flaw: ignoring the morning traffic.
The plan had one flaw because it ignored the morning traffic.
The plan had one flaw: it ignored the morning traffic.
questions.explanation: The colon introduces the explanatory clause it ignored the morning traffic, which specifies the flaw.
questions.skill: Punctuate an explanatory clause with a colon
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses causative have followed by an object and a bare infinitive?
choices: The coach had the team to practice the new formation.
The coach had the team practiced the new formation before the game.
The coach had the team practice the new formation.
The coach had that the team practice the new formation.
questions.explanation: Causative have can express the idea of causing someone to do something, as in had the team practice.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses an existential there construction with an indefinite plural subject and verb agreement?
choices: There were being several reasons for the delay.
There was several reasons for the delay.
There are several reason for the delay.
There were several reasons for the delay.
questions.explanation: The existential subject several reasons is plural, so the verb in the sentence is were.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly maintains parallel structure by using three simple-past action verbs?
choices: She packed sandwiches, filling water bottles, and checked the map.
She packed sandwiches, filled water bottles, and checked the map.
She packed sandwiches, filled water bottles, and was checking the map.
She packed sandwiches, filled water bottles, and the map.
questions.explanation: The verbs packed, filled, and checked are parallel simple-past verbs in the same grammatical form.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses nor to coordinate a negative clause and invert the auxiliary verb?
choices: The coach was not ready for the drill, nor was the players.
The coach was not ready for the drill, nor were the players.
The coach was not ready for the drill, and were the players.
The coach was not ready for the drill, nor the players were.
questions.explanation: Nor joins two negative clauses and correctly places were before the subject in the second clause.
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly adds an infinitive phrase to explain the purpose of rehearsing?
choices: The team rehearsed carefully for the avoidance of mistakes in the final performance.
The team rehearsed carefully so that mistakes would be avoided in the final performance.
The team rehearsed carefully because mistakes needed to be avoided in the final performance.
The team rehearsed carefully to avoid mistakes in the final performance.
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase to avoid mistakes in the final performance expresses the purpose of rehearsing.
questions.skill: Add an infinitive phrase of purpose
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence avoids a dangling participial phrase?
choices: The hikers returned, leaving the campsite was tidy.
Leaving the campsite tidy, the storm passed.
The hikers returned, leaving the campsite tidy.
Leaving the hikers tidy, the campsite was returned.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase leaving the campsite tidy logically modifies the hikers, the subject of returned.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a gerund phrase after the preposition without?
choices: Without check the schedule, the coach changed the practice time.
Without to check the schedule, the coach changed the practice time.
Without checked the schedule, the coach changed the practice time.
Without checking the schedule, the coach changed the practice time.
questions.explanation: The preposition without takes the gerund phrase checking the schedule, and the phrase correctly modifies the coach.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a restrictive relative clause to identify a particular coin?
choices: The archaeologist found a coin, which had been minted in the Roman colony.
The archaeologist found a coin that had been minted in the Roman colony.
The archaeologist found a coin which had minted in the Roman colony.
The archaeologist found a coin that was minted the Roman colony.
questions.explanation: The relative clause that had been minted in the Roman colony restricts the reference to a particular type of coin and contains a complete verb.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly forms an inverted conditional clause with were and a to-infinitive?
choices: Should archives to reopen next month, researchers might consult the letters.
Should the archives reopens next month, researchers might consult the letters.
Were the archives to reopen next month, researchers might consult the letters.
Should the archives to reopen next month, researchers might consult the letters.
questions.explanation: In the inverted conditional Were the archives to reopen, the subject follows the helping verb and the infinitive states the condition.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses whose to express possession within a relative clause?
choices: The student who proposal won the contest was invited to present it.
The student which proposal won the contest was invited to present it.
The student whose proposal won the contest was invited to present it.
The student whose proposal win the contest was invited to present it.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun whose expresses possession in the clause whose proposal won the contest.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses an absolute phrase to add information about the scene?
choices: With we set up the shelter, the tent flap fluttered in the wind.
With the tent flap fluttered in the wind, we set up the shelter.
With the tent flap fluttering in the wind, we set up the shelter.
With the tent flap in the wind, we set up the shelter.
questions.explanation: With the tent flap fluttering in the wind is an absolute phrase because it is grammatically independent of the subject we.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a noun clause functioning as the object of the preposition on?
choices: The decision rested on the proposal whether it met the budget.
The decision rested on whether the proposal met the budget.
Whether the proposal met the budget rested on the decision.
The decision rested on because the proposal met the budget.
questions.explanation: The noun clause whether the proposal met the budget serves as the object of the preposition on.
questions.skill: Using noun clauses as prepositional objects
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a semicolon to join two closely related independent clauses?
choices: The road was icy: we drove slowly.
Because the road was icy; we drove slowly.
The road was icy, we drove slowly.
The road was icy; we drove slowly.
questions.explanation: The semicolon properly joins the two independent clauses The road was icy and we drove slowly.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly embeds a question as a noun clause?
choices: The editor asked why was the manuscript delayed.
The editor asked why the manuscript had been delayed.
The editor asked the manuscript why it had been delayed.
The editor asked why the manuscript had delayed.
questions.explanation: The clause why the manuscript had been delayed functions as a noun clause and uses the normal subject-verb order of an embedded question.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses an appositive phrase to identify Ms. Ortiz's occupation?
choices: Ms. Ortiz, a ceramic artist taught the students to shape clay.
Ms. Ortiz, a ceramic artist, taught the students to shape clay.
Ms. Ortiz a ceramic artist, taught the students to shape clay.
Ms. Ortiz, was a ceramic artist, taught the students to shape clay.
questions.explanation: The phrase a ceramic artist is set off by commas as an appositive identifying Ms. Ortiz.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses inversion after the fronted negative adverbial hardly?
choices: Hardly the train had left the station when the signal changed.
Hardly had train left the station when the signal changed.
Hardly had the train left the station when the signal changed.
Hardly had the train left the station the signal changed.
questions.explanation: The fronted negative adverbial hardly requires subject-auxiliary inversion, placing had before the subject the train.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence has a compound predicate, with two coordinated verbs sharing the same subject?
choices: The librarian checked the catalog and wrote the new title on the board.
The librarian checked the catalog while writing the new title on the board.
After the librarian checked the catalog, she wrote the new title on the board.
The librarian checked the catalog before she wrote the new title on the board.
questions.explanation: The subject The librarian performs the coordinated verbs checked and wrote, which share the same subject.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses an if-clause to state a condition?
choices: Because the tickets sell out, the performance will be streamed online.
If the tickets sell out, the performance will be streamed online.
Although the tickets sell out, the performance will be streamed online.
When the tickets sell out, the performance will be streamed online.
questions.explanation: The if-clause states the condition under which the performance will be streamed online.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses not only...but also to coordinate exactly two parallel noun phrases?
choices: The teacher praised not only the careful draft but also praised the original idea.
The teacher praised not only the careful draft but also the original idea.
The teacher not only praised the careful draft but also the original idea.
The teacher praised not only the careful draft but also a original idea.
questions.explanation: The correlative pair not only...but also coordinates the two parallel noun phrases the careful draft and the original idea.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a gerund phrase as the complete subject?
choices: The detective's first step was reviewing the evidence.
That reviewing the evidence was the detective's first step.
Reviewing the evidence was the detective's first step.
The detective's first step was to reviewing the evidence.
questions.explanation: The gerund phrase Reviewing the evidence functions as the complete subject of the sentence.
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft
